To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the onset of the seizure sequence of myclonus, clonus and then hindlimb extension is related to brain levels of the convulsant agent, pentylenetrazol, in mice.

brain PTZ levels correlate with the onset of seizures in mice, that the brain PTZ uptake after S.C. injection was slower than after I.P. injections, and that the brain PTz uptake after S.C administration of PTZ CD40 was slower than the uptake after I.P. administration of PTZ.
the brain pentyleneterazol levels are related to seizure onset and that different routes of administration of pentylenetrazol affect the seizure onset.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for studying the mechanisms of seizure development.
the relationship of brain PTZ levels to seizure development and with the effects of different routes of PTZA administration on brain uptake and seizure development in mice.
the relationship between the PTZ-induced sequence of myoclenus, clonus, and hindlimb extention to brain PTZ level and the effects of different routes of administration on this relationship.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the onset of clonus and TE depends on brain PTZ concentration and that the onset of myoclonic jerks depends on a combination of brain PTZ concentration plus other factors that have not been determined.
brain PTZ levels are a necessary, but not sufficient, condition for the onset of seizures in the pentylenetrazol model of epilepsy.
brain PTZ levels are important in the onset of PTZ induced clonus and myoclonus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
brain PTZ levels and seizure onset times are dependent on the route of administration and that the onset of TE may be modulated by other factors.
the critical PTZ level for clonus onset was 20-50 microg/g, and that brain PTZ uptake after S.C. injection is slower than I.P. injection, but that the onset of clonus after S.C. PTZ is not delayed.
brain PTZ levels are an important determinant in seizure onset and that the seizure type (myoclonus or TE) may depend on the route of PTZ administration and on the rate of brain PTZ uptake.
The main takeaway from our work is that
brain PTZ uptake is rapid after I.P., and that brain PTZ levels are not the only determinant for TE.
brain PTZ uptake after S.C. injection is slower than that after I.P. administration.
brain PTZ levels are a critical component of the development of seizures in the PTZ model of epilepsy.
